item.title: MarketBeat Tracks News Sentiment and Media Coverage for Bank of New York Mellon
item.description:
MarketBeat Tracks News Sentiment and Media Coverage for Bank of New York Mellon

MarketBeat tracks and analyzes real-time media coverage and news sentiment for Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) alongside other finance companies. Utilizing automated tracking, the platform monitors headlines from more than one hundred trusted media outlets to gauge positive and negative press over rolling seven-day periods.

🔍 Overview

MarketBeat tracks news headlines from hundreds of media outlets and tags them by company. The system calculates a company news sentiment score based on the average sentiment of articles published about that company over the most recent seven days. This allows users to compare a specific company’s media coverage and sentiment against broader industry averages.

⚙️ Key details

The sentiment tracking system scores individual headlines and tracks overall engagement metrics for BNY.

  • Scoring System: Each tracked headline receives a score ranging from 2 (representing good news) to -2 (representing bad news).
  • Real-Time Tracking: The system continuously monitors articles, with the most recent headline for Bank of New York Mellon dated 10/2/2026.

item.title: MarketBeat updates company news sentiment scores for FNGR, TNON, ICFI, TXNM
item.description:
MarketBeat updates company news sentiment scores for FNGR, TNON, ICFI, TXNM

MarketBeat has refreshed its company news sentiment metrics, showing the latest seven‑day averages for four publicly traded firms.

🔍 Overview

  • MarketBeat tracks news headlines from hundreds of news outlets and tags them by company.
  • A sentiment score is assigned to each headline on a scale from -2 (bad news) to +2 (good news).
  • Company news sentiment scores represent the average of these headline scores over the most recent 7 days.
  • The system is used to identify companies that are receiving positive press.

⚙️ How it works

  • Headline scoring: Each headline receives a score ranging from 2 (good news) to -2 (bad news).
  • Aggregation: Scores are averaged across all articles about a company in the last seven days.
  • Comparison: A chart compares the number of articles about the company in the last seven days with the average number of articles in a typical week.
  • Media coverage: MarketBeat tracks news from more than one hundred trusted media outlets in real time (most recent ICF International headline dated 10/2/2026).

item.title: MarketBeat launches weekly company news sentiment scoring system
item.description:
MarketBeat launches weekly company news sentiment scoring system

MarketBeat has introduced a news sentiment scoring system that rates each headline on a scale from 2 (good news) to -2 (bad news) and tracks average sentiment for companies over the most recent 7 days.

🔍 Overview

  • Sentiment scores are calculated from headlines collected from hundreds of news outlets.
  • Scores help identify companies receiving positive or negative press.
  • The system also compares the number of articles published in the last week to a typical week.

⚙️ How it works

  • News headlines are tagged by company.
  • Each headline receives a score ranging from 2 (good) to -2 (bad).
  • Company news sentiment scores track the average sentiment of all articles about the company over the most recent 7 days.
  • The platform shows a sector‑average sentiment for context.

📊 Sample Metrics

  • Investors can gauge short‑term market perception of a company.
  • The sentiment metric provides a quick visual cue of news tone.
  • Comparing weekly article volume to the average helps spot spikes in media attention.
  • Sector‑level sentiment offers a benchmark for individual company scores.

item.title: New Completeness Estimation Approach Improves Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
item.description:
New Completeness Estimation Approach Improves Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

Researchers have introduced a new approach to improve multimodal sentiment analysis by addressing performance degradation caused by missing or noisy data in real-world scenarios.

🧩 How it works

The development introduces two primary components to handle incomplete data:

  • Completeness Estimation: An approach that quantifies the degree of sentiment-relevant information preserved in incomplete data to guide the reconstruction of missing semantics.
  • Training Strategy: A method designed to stabilize multi-task learning while jointly optimizing completeness estimation and sentiment prediction.

💡 Why it matters

Recent multimodal sentiment analysis studies often use text-centric fusion to exploit sentiment information in textual modalities. However, these approaches can suffer from performance degradation during inference when sentiment-related cues are missing or data is noisy.

⚙️ Key details

Experiments conducted on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that this approach results in:

  • More accurate semantic reconstruction.
  • More precise sentiment prediction.

#MultimodalAI #SentimentAnalysis #MachineLearning #DataReconstruction

Source: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Modalities via Semantic-aware Completeness based Reconstruction

item.title: C³T Transformer Enables Counterfactual Causal Reasoning of Sentiment Shifts in Social Media Threads
item.description:
C³T Transformer Enables Counterfactual Causal Reasoning of Sentiment Shifts in Social Media Threads

A new paper titled C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social‑Media Conversation Trees was submitted on 2 Sep 2026 to the Computer Science > Computation and Language category. The work tackles how sentiment changes throughout branching reply trees on social media, especially in rumor‑centric conversations.

🔍 Overview

  • Sentiment does not only vary across individual posts; it shifts as users react to claims, corrections, evidence, and hostility within a thread.
  • The authors treat discourse moves such as denial/correction, evidence/link, and toxicity/attack as candidate interventions.
  • Three research questions are posed:
    1. What sentiment does a reply express?
    2. Does the reply’s sentiment shift relative to its parent?
    3. Which prior message most plausibly drove the reply’s sentiment?

🧩 How it works

  • CaSiRe layer: A causal sentiment reasoning layer added to public rumor conversation datasets. It provides:
    • Post‑level sentiment labels
    • Parent‑child shift labels
    • Calibrated multi‑label intervention tags
    • Explicit causal‑source annotations
  • C$^{3}$T model (Counterfactual Causal Conversation Transformer):
    • Thread‑structured temporal architecture
    • Jointly predicts node sentiment and shift labels
    • Learns sparse ancestor attribution
    • Supports counterfactual queries by toggling intervention embeddings on or off to estimate potential outcomes

⚙️ Key Findings

  • Under an event‑level split, C$^{3}$T outperforms text‑only, graph‑based, and temporal baselines in out‑of‑event robustness and attribution accuracy.
  • Interpretable model effects show that:
    • Denials/corrections and evidence tend to reduce downstream negativity.
    • Toxicity tends to increase downstream negativity.
  • Open‑weight LLM prompting baselines benefit from added conversational context, but their attribution remains less reliable than the structure‑aware counterfactual approach.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a systematic way to attribute sentiment shifts to specific prior messages in complex conversation trees.
  • Enables researchers and platform moderators to simulate “what‑if” scenarios by turning interventions on or off, helping to assess potential mitigation strategies for harmful discourse.

The work demonstrates the value of combining causal reasoning with transformer‑based modeling for nuanced social‑media sentiment analysis.

#sentimentanalysis #causalAI #socialmedia #nlp

Source: C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees
